notes: Five examples chosen for diversity (illustration style, narration perspective, speaker type and visibility, speech emotion/speed) among non-NC samples whose baseline outputs show no reproduction of the ground truth. Every shown baseline produced all three outputs for each example.

examples.rationale: An older sibling narrates in the first person (“my baby brother Karthi”) but only watches: on the next page the narrator is out of frame while Savitha aunty plays with the baby and speaks, and Mom adjusts his nappy. Soft hand-painted illustrations on a warm beige ground.

A piggy bank narrates the story in the first person and is also the speaker. As Na sprinkles water over it, it says a sad, slow, low-pitched line about being apart from her, which the two-sentence narration only hints at. Soft digital painting.

The next page cuts from the children’s hands preparing vegetables to a close-up of a steaming pan with nobody in the frame, yet Fiza, out of view, speaks a delighted, high-pitched line about the sizzling spices that is not in the narration. Grainy illustrations with sketchy pencil lines.
A 60-word narration that recalls Maya being teased, illustrated as a three-panel composition. Her spoken line is a sad, slow inner monologue that does not appear in the narration.
Black-and-white line drawing on a colored frame. The next page's narration is only three words, and the image zooms from a wide shot to a close-up of Sam peering over the soup pot.
